$schema_note: Working PRD for the 'mote' issue+coordination tracker. Hand-edited; not bound to a JSON schema. Update this file (not tribal knowledge) when scope changes.

meta.name: mote
meta.tagline: Immutable op-maildir for one developer plus a few local agents.
meta.consolidates_note: This file is the authoritative working spec. The two source documents are kept as historical design rationale; any conflict between them and this file resolves to this file.

thesis.what_we_are_solving: Lightweight task + coordination tracking for a single workstation where one human and several local agents make tiny concurrent edits.
thesis.what_we_are_NOT_solving: Distributed multi-writer task graphs, server-mode databases, federation, cross-machine sync, or anything Beads/Dolt aim at.
why_op_maildir: Truth = create-only files. Writers never edit, truncate, or merge.
State = pure deterministic replay over filename-sorted ops.
Snapshots are disposable derived caches, never the source of truth.
Claims are TTL leases, not lock files.
Path coordination is advisory reservations, not real FS locks and not git skip-worktree.
what_we_avoid_by_construction: lock files on the main path
multi-step write transactions that can deadlock against themselves
any mutable cache that matters for correctness
the core re-entering itself via hooks

design_principles: Create-only publication: every mutation is a brand-new file in tmp/ then link()-ed into ops/.
Per-field clocks beat whole-row versions: scalar conflicts are deterministic, unrelated edits never collide.
Sets and append-only logs over scalars wherever possible (tags, deps, notes, messages).
Tombstones over hard-delete: stable IDs are worth more than literal deletion.
Rejected ops are retained as part of the audit trail; conflicts are visible, not silent.
Compound CLI commands publish a sequence of independent atomic ops; the CLI is responsible for compensating publishes on partial failure.
No daemon, no background task, no hook re-entry, no mutable shared cache.
non_goals_v1: Windows support (link() semantics + dir fsync portability).
Network filesystems / NFS (Maildir requires same local FS).
Built-in git integration (commits, hooks, post-merge triggers).
An always-on daemon or watcher process.
A query language beyond fixed CLI flags.
Git index manipulation, sparse-checkout flags, or automatic worktree creation.
Glob-style reservation paths (only exact-file or directory-prefix forms in v0.2).

platform.filesystem: POSIX local FS only. Same FS for tmp/ and ops/ is required (link() across FS is undefined-to-failing).
external_deps_intent: anyhow — error context for the CLI
blake3 — content hash for filename suffix
jiff — UTC timestamps with microsecond precision
rand — random 4-hex suffix in op filenames
ulid — bead / reservation / message / discussion-post ids
in_tree: Canonical JSON encoder (small RFC 8785-compatible subset; no external crate dependency).

layout..mote/tmp/: Maildir-style staging; only `mote fsck --clean-tmp` removes stragglers
layout..mote/ops/: immutable published ops, source of truth
layout..mote/local/: convenience state (e.g. `actor` file). Not source of truth.

write_protocol: 1. Build op struct; serialize to canonical JSON bytes.
5. link(.mote/tmp/<name>.json, .mote/ops/<name>.json). Errors on EEXIST -> hard fail (no silent overwrite).
6. Open .mote/ops/ as a directory; fsync(dir_fd); close(dir_fd). Required because fsync(file) does not durably commit the directory entry.
7. unlink(.mote/tmp/<name>.json). If unlink fails, log and continue: tmp/ debris is not a correctness issue.

fields.timestamp: UTC ISO-8601 basic compact form, microsecond precision, sortable lexicographically (e.g. 20260420T182455.124583Z)
fields.pid: process id, decimal, zero-padded to 4 chars min
fields.counter: per-process monotonic counter starting at 0 each process; 4 hex chars
fields.hash: first 6 hex chars (3 BLAKE3 bytes) over the canonical JSON of the op WITH the `op` field set to the empty string. Computable before being embedded; verifier recomputes identically.

storage.canonical_json: Sorted keys (lexicographic by UTF-16 code units, equivalent to byte order for ASCII keys), no insignificant whitespace, UTF-8 output. Implementation lives in-tree; we only emit booleans, integers, strings, arrays, and objects, so the full RFC 8785 number-canonicalization rules are not exercised.

ids.actor: Free-form short string, e.g. 'claude-fixer' or 'bbuchsbaum'. Resolved in this exact order: 1) --actor CLI flag, 2) MOTE_ACTOR env var, 3) .mote/local/actor file. No FORMAT.json fallback. No global config file in v1. If unresolved, mutating commands exit with code 3.
ids.store_resolution: Existing stores are resolved in this exact order: 1) --store CLI flag, 2) MOTE_STORE env var, 3) walk upward from cwd looking for .mote/. An explicit path may name the .mote directory or its parent.

storage.reading_state_v1: Scan .mote/ops/ once, sort filenames lexicographically, replay deterministically into an in-memory state struct. No snapshots, no inotify.

body.rule: Canonical summary only. Agent chatter belongs in notes, not body.

assignee.rule: Distinct from `claimed_by`. Assignee is intent (who should do it); claim is current TTL lease.

deps.rule: Blocking dependencies. Every dep edge kind blocks readiness for backward compatibility; cycles are accepted but `ready` won't fire on a node in a cycle of open beads.

rels.rule: Non-blocking relationships for hierarchy/containment. `ready` ignores these edges.

issue.purpose: Small mutable scalars + sets + append-only notes describing each bead.

path.purpose: Advisory TTL-bounded reservations over repo-relative paths so agents do not stomp each other's edits.
normalization_rules: Repo-relative only; absolute paths are rejected.
No `..` components; reject the op outright.
Use `/` as the separator internally regardless of host OS.
No symlink resolution; treat paths as lexical strings.
path.overlap_rule: Two paths overlap iff one is a prefix of the other under directory-component semantics. 'src/auth/' overlaps 'src/auth/token.rs' and 'src/auth/'; 'src/auth/' does NOT overlap 'src/authn/'.
path.compound_paths_in_one_op: If a single reserve_open lists both an exact file and a containing directory, treat both atoms as one logical reservation: all atoms must be free at op ts; otherwise the whole op is rejected.
path.boundary_with_git: Reservations are advisory; agents are expected to honor them. They are NOT real FS locks and NOT git skip-worktree (which is documented as for sparse checkout and may be overwritten on merge/rebase). For genuine HEAD/index isolation, use a git worktree — that boundary is intentional and out of scope for mote.

message.purpose: Durable direct messages with receipt acknowledgement and a correlated request/reply lifecycle.

discussion.purpose: Public cross-agent message board for strategy, coordination, and discussion that is not tied to issue lodging.

event_projection.purpose: Read-only, versioned incremental delivery of accepted durable operations to local harnesses without adding a broker, daemon, or event operation kind.
event_projection.event_id: The accepted operation id/filename stem. It is also the resume and deduplication cursor.
event_projection.delivery: One JSON object per line; filesystem notifications for normal delivery plus a periodic full-directory fallback scan.
event_projection.resume: --after <event-id> replays matching operations later in deterministic filename order, then follows when requested.
event_projection.source_of_truth: Events are disposable projections. Only immutable files in ops/ are durable truth.

op_envelope.op: op id (string equal to the filename without .json)
op_envelope.ts: RFC3339 UTC timestamp with microsecond precision; MUST equal the timestamp embedded in the filename
op_envelope.kind: one of: create | patch | tag_add | tag_remove | dep_add | dep_remove | rel_add | rel_remove | note | claim | release | close | delete | reserve_open | reserve_close | msg_send | msg_ack | msg_resolve | board_topic | board_post | board_sticky | board_read

fields.set: { title, status?, priority?, body?, assignee? }  (scalars only; tags/deps/rels go through tag_add/dep_add/rel_add)

create.reducer: Accepted iff no prior accepted `create` exists for entity. On accept, every set field's clock becomes this op id.

fields.expect: { field_name -> expected current clock op_id, or null for never-written }

patch.reducer: Scalar-only patch. Accepted iff for every field f in `expect`, current `_clock[f] == expect[f]`. On accept: each field in `set` updates its clock to this op id.
patch.rejection: If any expect mismatches, the entire op is rejected and recorded as a rejected intent. No partial application.

tag_add.reducer: Idempotent. Accepted if entity exists and is not deleted. Adds tag to the bead's tag set.

tag_remove.reducer: Idempotent. Accepted if entity exists and is not deleted. Removes tag from the bead's tag set; no-op if absent.

fields.dep_kind: string  (default 'blocks'). Named `dep_kind` (not `kind`) so it does not collide with the envelope's `kind` tag.

dep_add.reducer: Idempotent. Accepted if both entities exist and are not deleted; rejected if entity == parent (self-dependency).

dep_remove.reducer: Idempotent. Accepted if both entities exist; no-op if the edge is absent.

fields.rel_kind: string  (default 'parent'). Named `rel_kind` (not `kind`) so it does not collide with the envelope's `kind` tag.

rel_add.reducer: Idempotent. Accepted if both entities exist and are not deleted; rejected if entity == parent (self-relation). Does not affect readiness.

rel_remove.reducer: Idempotent. Accepted if both entities exist; no-op if the edge is absent. Does not affect readiness.

note.reducer: Always accepted if the target entity exists. Append-only. Notes carry no `expect` field — they are intentionally low-friction.
note.rationale: Splits 'progress chatter' off from `body` (a canonical summary), so multiple agents can leave updates on one bead without text-merge conflicts.

fields.expect: { status?: op_id }  optional; if present, current `_clock.status` must match

close.reducer: Sets status = 'closed' and updates _clock.status to this op id. If `expect.status` is provided and mismatches current clock, rejected. Closing an already-closed bead is a no-op success.

delete.reducer: Accepted iff entity exists and is not already deleted. Sets deleted_at = this op's ts. Bead is hidden from `ls`/`show` defaults; `history` still includes it.

fields.to: actor receiving the claim (often == op.actor on first claim, or new actor on handoff)
fields.ttl_s: integer seconds; defaults to FORMAT.json default_ttl_s.claim
fields.expect_claim: optional op_id of expected current claim_clock

claim.reducer: Accepted iff (current claim is absent or expired by this op's ts) OR `expect_claim` == current claim_clock. On accept: claim_clock = this op id, claimed_by = `to`, lease_until = this.ts + ttl_s.

fields.expect_claim: optional op_id of expected current claim_clock

release.reducer: Accepted iff op.actor == current claimed_by OR `expect_claim` == current claim_clock. On accept: claim cleared, claim_clock advanced to this op id.

fields.entity: bd-<ULID>  (the issue this reservation supports; required)
fields.paths: [repo-relative path strings]; trailing slash means directory; subject to normalization rules in planes.path
fields.ttl_s: integer seconds; defaults to FORMAT.json default_ttl_s.reservation

reserve_open.reducer: All-or-nothing. Accepted iff no live reservation by a different actor overlaps any listed path at this op's ts. A live reservation is one whose lease_until = open_op.ts + ttl_s has not been exceeded by this op's ts AND which has not been closed by a later reserve_close referencing the same reservation_id.
reserve_open.rejection: If any path conflicts, the whole op is rejected; no partial reservation is opened.

fields.reservation_id: rv-<ULID> of the reserve_open being closed
fields.paths: optional [path]; default = all paths in the referenced reservation

reserve_close.reducer: Accepted iff the referenced reservation exists and op.actor == owner. Idempotent for already-closed paths.

fields.entity: optional bd-<ULID>; messages may be issue-scoped
fields.reservation: optional rv-<ULID>; messages may reference a reservation
fields.msg_kind: note | request | response | decline | handoff | blocked | fyi
fields.reply_to: optional root request msg_id; required for response and decline
fields.correlation_id: optional stable request conversation id; request roots default to their msg_id and replies inherit it

msg_send.reducer: Accepted when msg_id is unique, any idempotency_key is unused by op.actor, and optional entity exists. Legacy request ops without correlation metadata replay as open requests with correlation_id = msg_id. A response/decline is accepted only from the addressed recipient, targets the root sender, inherits request context/correlation, and the request is still open; it advances derived request state to responded/declined. Self-send is allowed but discouraged.

msg_ack.reducer: Accepted iff op.actor == referenced msg_send.to AND no prior msg_ack from op.actor for this msg_id. Self-ack of one's own send is rejected. Ack means receipt/seen only and never changes request_state.

msg_resolve.reducer: Accepted iff op.actor is the request sender and derived request_state is responded or declined. Advances the request to resolved. Open requests and repeated resolution are rejected.

fields.title: optional display title; defaults to topic

board_topic.reducer: Accepted iff topic is non-empty and no explicit topic with the same identity already exists. A topic created implicitly by an earlier board_post may be upgraded to explicit.

fields.topic: single-line topic string; default CLI topic is `general`

board_post.reducer: Append-only. Accepted iff post_id is unique, topic/body are non-empty, and reply_to (when present) references an already accepted board_post. If the topic does not exist, replay creates an implicit topic summary.

board_sticky.reducer: Accepted iff post_id references an accepted board_post. Sticky state is last-writer-wins in replay order; topic sticky_count and last_activity are updated from accepted sticky changes.

fields.upto_op_id: op id of an accepted board_post
fields.topic: optional topic for a topic-scoped read cursor

board_read.reducer: Accepted iff upto_op_id references an accepted board_post and, when topic is present, the referenced post belongs to that topic. On accept, advances op.actor's global or topic-scoped discussion read cursor monotonically. `discuss unread` lists accepted board_post ops newer than the applicable cursor, excluding the actor's own posts.

reducer.ordering: Strict lexicographic order of filenames in .mote/ops/. Filenames are designed to sort to the same order as wall-clock publication.
reducer.determinism: Two replays over the same set of files MUST produce identical state. No randomness, no clock reads during replay.
reducer.rejection_handling: Rejected ops remain in .mote/ops/. The reducer records the reason. `mote history --include-rejected` exposes them. The CLI command that published the op exits 2.
reducer.snapshots_v0_3_plus: If profiling later demands it, snapshots may be written to .mote/snap/<frontier-op-id>.json. They are derived caches: any inconsistency is resolved by deleting the snapshot and replaying. Never authoritative. Not in v0.2.

concurrency_model.scalar_field_clocks: Each scalar field carries an op_id of its last accepted writer. A `patch` must declare expectations matching current clocks for every field it sets. Two patches to disjoint fields both succeed.
concurrency_model.set_fields: tag_add/tag_remove/dep_add/dep_remove/rel_add/rel_remove are commutative and idempotent. No clocks needed.
concurrency_model.append_only: Notes and ordinary msg_send ops never conflict. Sender-scoped idempotency keys deduplicate retries; structured replies race on the root request's open state. msg_ack and msg_resolve are one-shot transitions.
concurrency_model.claim_leases: TTL-bounded; expired leases auto-yield to the next claim. Stale agents do not leave permanent locks.
concurrency_model.path_reservations: TTL-bounded advisory leases. Overlap rule prevents two actors from believing they own the same code area. v0.2 supports only `exclusive` mode. Honor is voluntary by convention; a non-cooperating writer is out of scope.

module_layout.src/main.rs: binary entry; argv parsing dispatch only
module_layout.src/op.rs: typed op envelope + per-kind structs + serde
module_layout.src/publish.rs: tmp write + sync + hardlink publish + dir fsync
module_layout.src/reducer.rs: replay rules: accept/reject decisions per op kind
module_layout.src/events.rs: versioned event envelopes, category/actor filters, op cursors, and shared filesystem/fallback follow primitive
module_layout.src/watch.rs: read-only board snapshots driven by the shared follow primitive
module_layout.src/query.rs: ls / show / ready / history / inbox / who-has / board
module_layout.src/fsck.rs: filename + hash + JSON validation; tmp/ cleanup

global_flags.--actor <s>: override actor identity for this invocation
global_flags.--store <dir>: override store path (then MOTE_STORE; default: walk up from cwd looking for .mote/)

commands.name: init
commands.description: Create .mote/ in the current dir if absent; write FORMAT.json; create tmp/, ops/, local/. Idempotent.

commands.name: actor
commands.synopsis: mote actor set|show|clear ... | mote actor list
commands.description: Manage the shared local actor convenience file or derive known actors from accepted activity, message recipients, claims, and reservations. actor list is read-only and reports last activity plus current coordination counts.

commands.name: new
commands.synopsis: mote new "<title>" [-p N] [--body STR] [--tag T]... [--dep ID]...
commands.description: Publish a `create` op (plus tag_add/dep_add ops for any --tag / --dep). Prints the new bd-id.

commands.name: set
commands.description: Publish a scalar `patch` op. expect clocks are taken from the current replayed state at command time. Multiple field=value pairs allowed; all packed into one op. Exit 2 on conflict.

commands.name: show
commands.description: Render full bead state (scalars + tags + deps + relations + notes + claim + active reservations), including downward relation children and blocking dependents.

commands.name: ls
commands.description: List beads. Default: open beads. Multiple --tag filters are an intersection. `--ready` is equivalent to `mote ready`.

commands.name: ready
commands.description: List beads that are open + have no open blocking deps + are not currently claimed by another actor.

commands.name: history
commands.description: Print all ops touching this entity in filename order. Default omits rejected ops; `--include-rejected` includes them with their rejection reason.

commands.name: dep
commands.description: Manage blocking deps. Publishes one `dep_add` or `dep_remove` op. Containment-looking kinds such as `parent` warn at the CLI but still block for compatibility.

commands.name: rel
commands.description: Manage non-blocking relationships for hierarchy/containment. Publishes one `rel_add` or `rel_remove` op.

commands.name: parents
commands.description: List non-blocking relation parents of a bead.

commands.name: children
commands.description: List non-blocking relation children of a bead.

commands.name: dependents
commands.description: List beads blocked by this bead through dependency edges.

commands.name: tag
commands.synopsis: mote tag add <id> <tag>... | mote tag rm <id> <tag>
commands.description: Manage tags. `tag add` can publish multiple `tag_add` ops in one invocation.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Read JSONL batch actions and publish ordinary ops sequentially, reporting accepted/rejected/skipped results.

commands.name: import
commands.description: Read a JSON plan with beads, deps, and relations and publish ordinary ops sequentially.

commands.name: note
commands.description: Append-only note. note_kind in: note | progress | decision | handoff | blocker.

commands.name: close
commands.description: Publish a `close` op. Sets status=closed. Idempotent.

commands.name: claim
commands.description: Publish a `claim` op.

commands.name: release
commands.description: Publish a `release` op.

commands.name: reserve
commands.description: Publish a `reserve_open` op. Exit 2 on overlap.

commands.name: unreserve
commands.description: Publish a `reserve_close` op.

commands.name: preflight
commands.description: Dry run. Reports any reservation overlaps. Exit 0 if free, exit 2 if any conflict.

commands.name: begin
commands.description: Compound: publishes `reserve_open`, then `claim`, then optional `note`. On reserve_open conflict: exit 2 immediately, no further ops. On claim conflict after reservation: emit compensating `reserve_close` and exit 2.

commands.name: handoff
commands.description: Compound: publishes a handoff `note`, then a reassigning `claim` to <actor>, then `reserve_close` for current actor's reservations on the issue (only if --release).

commands.name: done
commands.description: Compound: publishes a completion `note` (note_kind=note), `close`, then `reserve_close` for current actor's reservations on the issue, then `release` of any current claim by this actor.

commands.name: inbox
commands.synopsis: mote inbox [--issue ID] [--from ACTOR] [--kind K] [--wait [--timeout S] | --follow [--after EVENT]]
commands.description: List msg_send ops with to == self.actor and no msg_ack from self. Wait mode returns pending messages or blocks once for a matching delivery and exits, preserving ordinary inbox output shape. Follow mode streams deliveries with compact human output or versioned JSON events; --after resumes JSON/event consumption from an event id.

commands.name: msg
commands.synopsis: mote msg send --to <actor> [--issue ID] [--reservation RV] [--kind K] [--idempotency-key KEY] "<text>"  |  mote msg reply <request-id> [--kind response|decline] [--idempotency-key KEY] "<text>"  |  mote msg requests [--state STATE]  |  mote msg ack|resolve <msg-id>
commands.description: Publish direct messages, acknowledge receipt, correlate request replies, query derived request state, and resolve completed request lifecycles.

commands.name: discuss
commands.synopsis: mote discuss topic new <topic> [--title T] [--body B]  |  mote discuss post [--topic TOPIC] [--reply-to POST] "<text>"  |  mote discuss sticky|unsticky <post-id>  |  mote discuss list [--topic TOPIC] [--limit N]  |  mote discuss search <query> [--topic TOPIC] [--limit N]  |  mote discuss unread [--topic TOPIC] [--limit N]  |  mote discuss mark-read [--topic TOPIC]  |  mote discuss replies <post-id>  |  mote discuss thread <post-id>  |  mote discuss topics
commands.description: Publish and read public cross-agent message-board topics, posts, sticky state, replies, thread views, search results, activity summaries, and per-actor unread state.

commands.name: who-has
commands.description: List live reservations whose paths overlap <path>.

commands.name: board
commands.description: Compact overview: counts by status, current claims, current reservations, recent notes, unread inbox count.

commands.name: events
commands.synopsis: mote events [--kind K,...] [--for-actor A] [--after EVENT] [--follow] [--interval S]
commands.description: Emit accepted operations as mote.event.v1 JSONL/human events. --follow waits via filesystem notifications with periodic fallback; no operations are published.

commands.name: fsck
commands.description: Verify filename hash suffixes and (with --clean-tmp) remove stragglers from .mote/tmp/. Does NOT heal locks; does NOT alter ops/.

exit_codes.2: op rejected by reducer (stale, overlap, already-acked, etc.)
exit_codes.3: invalid command, validation error, or actor identity unresolved

v1_scope: Verify each filename's hash suffix matches BLAKE3-6 of the canonical JSON of the op (with `op` field temporarily blanked).
Report any filename that does not parse against the op_naming format.
Report any duplicate op_ids in ops/ (should be impossible if link()-with-EEXIST contract holds, but verify).
explicitly_out_of_scope: Heuristic 'is this stale file safe to delete' on ops/ (NEVER delete published ops).
Re-deriving snapshots (handled separately if/when snapshots ship).

git_boundary.stance: mote stays out of git. Mote files (.mote/) MAY be committed, but mote does not run git, install hooks, or read git state.
git_boundary.worktree_advice: When two agents truly need separate HEAD/index, use `git worktree add`. That is the right escape hatch. mote's path reservations are for in-place collaboration on a single working tree.

milestones.name: Storage primitives
deliverables: Walk-up `.mote/` discovery; `mote init` writes FORMAT.json and creates tmp/, ops/, local/.
Canonical JSON encoder (in-tree).
Op naming + parse + filename comparator (with 6-hex content hash).
publish_op(): O_CREAT|O_EXCL on tmp, fsync(file), link to ops, fsync(dir), unlink(tmp).
Replay loop: read dir, sort, deserialize.
Hash verification for fsck.
milestones.exit_criteria: Acceptance test A3 passes. Unit tests cover canonical JSON, op naming round-trip, store discovery. Crash-injection harness in tests/ shows no half-published op surfaces in ops/.

milestones.name: Issue plane — scalars, tags, deps, relations
deliverables: Op kinds: create, patch, tag_add, tag_remove, dep_add, dep_remove, rel_add, rel_remove, close, delete.
Reducer with per-field clocks.
CLI: init, new, set, show, ls, history, dep, rel, parents, children, dependents, tag, batch, import, close, fsck.
milestones.exit_criteria: Acceptance tests A1, A2, A9 pass.

milestones.name: Issue plane — notes & ready
deliverables: note op + reducer.
ready computation (open + no open blockers + not foreign-claimed).
CLI: note, ready (and `ls --ready` alias).
milestones.exit_criteria: Acceptance test A8 passes; ready returns the expected frontier on a hand-built dep graph.

milestones.name: Claims & messages
deliverables: claim, release, msg_send, msg_ack ops + reducers.
CLI: claim, release, msg send, msg ack, inbox.

milestones.name: Path plane (coordination layer)
deliverables: Path overlap helper with prefix-component semantics + normalization rules.
reserve_open, reserve_close ops + reducer with all-or-nothing accept.
Compound CLI: preflight, begin, handoff, done with compensating reserve_close.
Query CLI: who-has, board, reserve, unreserve.
milestones.exit_criteria: Acceptance tests A4, A7 pass; compound-failure behavior documented and tested.

milestones.name: Polish & robustness
deliverables: fsck full surface, JSON output mode (--json), better diagnostics on rejection (which field clock mismatched, which path overlapped).
README + man-page-style docs for each command.
milestones.exit_criteria: Acceptance test A10 passes; manual end-to-end script covering all CLI commands runs clean.

milestones.name: Incremental event delivery
deliverables: Read-only mote.event.v1 envelopes with stable event ids, full kind payloads, category filters, actor relevance filters, and resume cursors.
Shared filesystem notification plus periodic fallback primitive used by watch and event follow surfaces.
CLI: events [--follow], inbox --follow, and --after cursor replay.
milestones.exit_criteria: Acceptance test A15 passes; schema, cursor, actor filter, initial inbox, notification latency, and fallback behavior have automated coverage.

milestones.name: Structured request and reply lifecycle
deliverables: Backward-compatible optional reply_to, correlation_id, and sender-scoped idempotency_key fields on msg_send.
Reducer-derived open, responded, declined, and resolved request states with receipt-only acknowledgement semantics.
msg_resolve op plus CLI: msg reply, msg requests, msg resolve, and idempotent send/reply retries.
milestones.exit_criteria: Acceptance test A16 passes; legacy replay, participant permissions, acknowledgement independence, response/decline transitions, resolution, idempotency conflict, JSON query, and message event coverage are automated.

milestones.name: Terminal messaging ergonomics
deliverables: MOTE_STORE environment routing with explicit --store precedence for shared coordination across worktrees.
Read-only actor list derived from accepted activity and coordination state without registration or heartbeats.
Bounded inbox --wait plus compact human follow output, reusing the existing event tailer.
Canonical agent guidance for per-terminal MOTE_ACTOR identities and inbox checks at coordination boundaries.
milestones.exit_criteria: Acceptance test A17 passes; environment precedence, actor JSON shape, pending/timeout/new-delivery wait behavior, and human follow output have automated coverage without op-schema changes.

acceptance_tests.name: Concurrent creates
acceptance_tests.spec: Spawn 20 processes that each `mote new`. All 20 succeed; .mote/ops/ contains 20 distinct create ops with 20 distinct bead ids; replay produces 20 beads.

acceptance_tests.name: Same-field race
acceptance_tests.spec: From identical observed state, two processes race `mote set <id> status=doing`. Exactly one exits 0; the other exits 2 with a clock-mismatch reason. Both ops persist in ops/. Replay shows only one accepted patch.
source_alignment: mote_prd.md §28 integration: concurrent patch on same field

acceptance_tests.name: Crash before publish
acceptance_tests.spec: SIGKILL a writer between fsync(tmp) and link(). On restart, ops/ contains no new file; tmp/ contains the orphan; `mote fsck --clean-tmp` removes it.

acceptance_tests.name: Reservation overlap
acceptance_tests.spec: Two agents race `mote begin` on overlapping paths (e.g. src/auth/ vs src/auth/token.rs). Exactly one succeeds; the other exits 2 with overlap report. The losing agent emits no claim.

acceptance_tests.name: Claim lease expiry
acceptance_tests.spec: Agent A claims with ttl=1. After 2s of wall-clock, agent B claims and succeeds.

acceptance_tests.name: Inbox round-trip
acceptance_tests.spec: alice msg_send to bob; bob inbox lists it; bob ack; bob inbox is empty; alice's history shows the msg + ack.

acceptance_tests.name: Path overlap correctness
